xlg05_transfer_prior.description: XLG-05 (WP25): does a CFB-anchored PRIOR on the NFL residual model's coefficients beat shrink-toward-zero? Four arms on the IDENTICAL 14-column shared feature subset S (the measured CFB/NFL contract intersection, ALIGNED_TRANSFER_FEATURE_COLUMNS), all at the frozen ridge_alpha=10.0 against market_residual: (a) NFL-only ridge on S = BASELINE; (b) naive pooled control, one ridge on NFL+CFB rows with a league indicator; (c) CFB-pretrained, theta_cfb as the ridge prior MEAN; (d) partially pooled, prior mean kappa*theta_cfb with kappa chosen by leave-one-season-out on TRAINING seasons only over the frozen grid {0,.25,.5,.75,1} (kappa=0 IS arm a, kappa=1 IS arm c). No arm sees a column another does not, so this tests a MODEL change (a prior on the estimator), NOT a team-quality feature - the owner's 'team quality is already priced' bound is checked explicitly by a prior_market_only diagnostic arm that forbids the prior from touching any EPA coefficient. Close-graded screen, walk-forward weekly, min_train_games=50, paired forced-pick accuracy delta in accuracy_points, week-blocked primary. Predeclared in docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md before any outcome number. No inheritance: a new mechanism hypothesis, not a variant of any feature family in the ledger.

windows.notes: Window [2011,2013] spent on the XLG-05 four-arm CFB->NFL coefficient-prior screen, close-graded, predeclared in docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md. This verdict carries ARM (d) partial_pooled's numbers, a choice declared in the predeclaration BEFORE the numbers existed: the ledger records one verdict per window and arm (d) is the family's headline mechanism -- the only arm that adapts its prior strength to the data, and one that strictly contains arms (a) and (c) as the endpoints of its own kappa grid. Arm (d) is an EXACT TIE with the NFL-only baseline: 0 of 746 paired non-push games change pick, both at 50.938%, so the interval is a point mass at [0,0] and probability_positive 0.500 is the tie-aware value (a dead heat is EV-neutral; the raw mean(draws>0) of 0.000 would misreport it as a certain loss -- docs/xlg05_transfer_prior.md section 6a). Companion arms, same window, recorded as weak signals: (b) naive_pooled +0.000 pts, 220 picks differing split exactly 110/110, tie-aware P+ 0.522; (c) cfb_prior +0.134 pts, week 95% CI [-0.669,+0.926], tie-aware P+ 0.652 (season-blocked 0.860) on just 7 differing picks. Reference line, reported not compared: full production weak_stack scores 49.866% on these same 746 games vs the 14-column nfl_only arm's 50.938% -- but 7 of production's 90 model columns (lineup continuity) have 0% coverage in 2009-2012 and 87.5% in 2013, so production runs this window with part of its feature set inert, and 2011-2013 sits outside the seasons it was built on. Positive control passed decisively (leaked baseline 100.00%, candidates -49 pts, P+ 0.000, 366 of 746 picks differing). NOTHING CLOSES: no resolved wrong sign, and no_split_half_reliability was ruled out in the predeclaration because these arms differ in the ESTIMATOR, not in a feature, so no trait exists to split. Two follow-ups, each a NEW predeclaration: (1) a declared prior-strength/alpha sweep -- at alpha=10 the prior shifts home_cover_probability by at most 0.016, and this run REFUTES docs/scaling_and_transfer.md's written expectation that alpha=10 would bind harder on NFL's smaller training sets; (2) re-measure on an S with its three exact collinearities (diff = home - away) removed, since theta_cfb is anti-correlated between odd and even CFB seasons (r=-0.5333), which that redundancy plausibly explains.
